content.text: Breaking News More (-1) » Local Sports Gonzaga Head Coach Mark Few officially named to Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2026 Mark Few, Gonzaga Head Basketball Coach, has officially been named as a part of the 2026 class of Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame. Few is one of nine inductees. The man who has led Gonzaga basketball for 27 years has just received one of the highest honors. Author: Grace Uppendahl Published: 10:56 AM PDT April 4, 2026 Updated: 10:57 AM PDT April 4, 2026 SPOKANE, Wash. — Mark Few, Gonzaga head basketball coach, is officially named as a part of the 2026 class of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame. Few is one of nine inductees who will be celebrated during the Enshrinement festivities August 14-15, 2026. The announcement of the 2026 class was made during the Men's Final Four weekend of the NCAA March Madness Tournament in Indianapolis, according to the press release. Few is "one of the most successful coaches in college basketball history, Few has led Gonzaga to sustained national prominence," according to the press release. The Naismith Basketball Hall of fame also describes him as "the winningest active coach by winning percentage." Few has ensured the Zags' invitation to the NCAA March Madness tournament every year he has been head coach. Other inductees for the North America Committee include Joey Crawford, Doc Rivers and Amar'e Stoudemire. The 2026 class will be honored during festivities in Springfield, Massachusetts on August 14-15. Tickets and packages are available at this website. "Everyone is playing for their own tribe, that's why it’s called Battle of the Nations and there is a lot of pride in it as well," said Jerry Ford, the tournament director. "So playing with your family against another tribe...going off to battle." Organizers said there will be 84 men's teams, 37 women's teams, and 105 youth teams facing off on the court in Spokane this weekend. The tournament is also a celebration of culture and community. "It's really amazing how everyone comes together, and we get to visit and see each other," Battle of the Nations Association treasurer Maria Cullooyah said. "Families that live so far apart get to come to Spokane and see one another and catch up, break some bread, and have some fun!" The Battle of the Nations tournament tips off at 8am Friday at the HUB Sports Center in Liberty Lake. "Not everyone is a dancer or drummer like you see at the powwows, so this is like a culture because basketball is big in Indian country and it's getting all together and visiting with friends," said Ford. "A lot of these people, a lot of tribes know each other and it's kind of just bringing everyone together."
